newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols firm as market stays wary.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols firm as market stays wary.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options held firm in quiet U.S. trading Friday as the market remained on the alert for more sharp movements in the spot, traders said.
"The market is still concerned about further yen selling," said Soma Rao, options sales manager for Smith Barney Inc in New York.
The dollar was bid at 115.65 yen in the U.S. afternoon, having recovered from a couple of early forays below 115.00.

Dollar/yen vols were slightly higher across the curve, with one-month at 11.8/12.1 percent, up from 11.6/11.7 percent Thursday, two-month up about 0.2 point at 10.9/11.2 percent and one-year also gaining 0.2 point to 10.0/10.3 percent.

Dealers who became short gamma as a result of the high demand for yen calls from Japanese corporations as the dollar tanked have been continuously covering those positions, keeping volatility underpinned, said Alan Revercomb, options strategist for I.D.E.A. Inc.

In just two weeks, the dollar has lost more than 10 percent of its value versus the yen, sparked by concern about higher Japanese interest rates and a stream of comments from Japanese officials in defense of the yen.

Persistent interest in buying dollar puts and yen calls was still being reflected in the one-month 25-delta dollar/yen risk reversal, which were strongly skewed toward yen calls at 1.0/1.4, options traders said.
In addition, they said, market participants were setting up spread trades to take advantage of the lower volatilities in dollar/mark.

Revercomb said one-month dollar/yen volatility would push back above 12.0 percent, revisiting highs seen this week, if the spot were to drop below 114.80 yen, while a return to levels above 116.00 would be necessary to cool it.
The obsession with dollar/yen has completely overshadowed dollar/mark, traders said.
"Dollar/mark is in the backseat, trading with no real direction to it," said Rao.
One-month dollar/mark volatility edged 0.1 point higher to 9.1/9.4 percent, but two-month was steady at 8.9/9.2 percent and one-year declined slightly to 8.7/9.0 percent.
The 25-delta risk reversal for one-month dollar/mark options was little changed at 0.1/0.4 in favor of mark calls.
Rao said dollar/mark could garner support next week and ultimately revisit the 1.71 area if the Federal Open Market Committee boosts short-term rates at its meeting Tuesday.
Analysts are split on the prospects for another 25-basis-point increase in the federal funds rate.
However, a U.S. rate hike next week would have little impact on dollar/yen, Rao said. "Dollar/yen is a different story. Dollar/yen could be anywhere" next week, he said.
